opening.spoken: This record covers the claimed solution of The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis: what has been claimed, what it rests on, and what would have to be checked by whom.

short_version.spoken: On 20 November 2026 Ravi Vakil posted a 940-page draft by Alessandro Maria Masullo, titled The Music of the Primes, saying that Masullo has a proposed proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, that Brian Conrad has read it closely for months and that it is "so far looking good", that it is "all human, with no AI", and asking people to check it, formalize it and fill small gaps. The author's preface says the work took twelve years, that "the math is complete" and only writing remains, and that he and Conrad know of "several glitches". The draft is unfinished where it matters most: Chapter 13, which is to deduce the location of the zeros from the trace formula of Chapter 12, is two pages of headings with footnotes reading "Insert statement" and "State and prove the Main Theorems". A third-party Lean formalization effort began the same day and paused the same day over a disputed main formula. Everything here is open.

what_happened.spoken: The claim was pinned from the public record: the problem page, the proof-claims thread, and every artifact the claimants made public, by commit or hash. Nothing was run. The gaps that follow are the checks still owed.

cycles.spoken: The author's preface says an overview of the methods was sent in a letter to Peter Sarnak in mid-October 2026, excerpts of which are in the draft, and that he and Brian Conrad visited Sarnak for a blackboard discussion on the Sunday before release. Ravi Vakil posted the draft at 10:18 in the blog's local time, writing that Brian Conrad has read it closely for months, that it is so far looking good, that it is all human with no AI, and asking readers to check and formalize it. The PDF served from the post is 940 pages and 6,756,996 bytes, last modified 18:18 UTC. A third-party Lean 4 formalization repository was created at 18:43 UTC and was marked on hold the same day, its README reporting a dispute over the trace formula and its errata file listing problems found in the appendices. Nervous Machine fetched the PDF at 22:18 UTC; its hash matches the one the formalization repository records.

public_reactions.who: Hassana Labs (Leon Chlon), by a reinforcement-learning "verified debate" model over one weekend
public_reactions.what: Reports 44 issues in the 940-page draft, 23 of them not raised in any public review before, each with a proposed repair: 15 repairs proved in Lean, 5 with key pieces in Lean, 2 on paper, 1 absorbed by another. Gives what it calls an exact diagnosis, proved in Lean: in the corrected trace formula behind Theorem 12.5.1.1 the remainder is independent of the strip width if and only if every zero lies on Re = 1/2, so the argument's central step is equivalent to its conclusion. Confirms that section 12.3 reads "Include section", that the proof of 10.4.2.8 ends "Return here and complete proof", and that Theorem 13.3.1.2 has no statement. Reports new mathematics built alongside: the geometric side in the operator order P∘A at every finite rank, the missing section 12.3 decomposition, a nuclearity bound, a spectral converse, and foundations; about 80,000 lines of Lean in all. Of the nine results the argument relies on, each is listed with what is proved and what is "not yet", including: no continuation and functional equation for number fields other than Q; the identity of P∘A(h) with the assembled operator not yet proved; Theorem 12.4.1.1 as a whole not yet stated. Opens by congratulating the author. Lean 4.27.0-rc1, Mathlib commit fdddb3e; 1,506 declarations named, 1,393 with receipts showing exit code 0 and the three standard axioms, 26 turned back by their compile service for linter warnings only, 87 definitions inside checked files. Each source is a standalone compilation unit; the README says different sources may declare the same names.
public_reactions.note: The reader is a model and the signature is a company's, so this is a report, not a read cycle: it does not close the reading gap, and it is not a specialist's check of anything. What the Lean checks is the reviewers' own statements, not the manuscript's: the key theorem, remainder_independent_iff_critical_line in lean/spectral/Proof-28b15828da3e/Proof.lean (receipt-1.json: exit code 0, 106 s, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; source hash matches), is about an arbitrary entire function f with a zero count O(R log R), takes the corrected trace formula as a hypothesis in the form "the sum over zeros within width a of the line tends to G minus remainder(a)", and concludes that the remainder is the same for all widths if and only if f has no zero off the line. Read plainly: if the trace formula is of that form, then the step the draft would need is a restatement of the conclusion. The Chapter 13 statement for K = Q, chapter13_paired_control_iff_riemannHypothesis, is likewise conditional on an interface (Chapter13RegularizedLimit D) and concludes Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis from a control condition and back. Both are machine-checked diagnoses of the argument's shape; neither proves or refutes the trace formula on the draft's actual objects. On this record: no formal deduction of the main theorem exists (EG1 unchanged); no independent mathematician has read the draft under their name (EG2 unchanged); the author has not released Chapter 13 (EG3 unchanged, and the report confirms the placeholders page by page); the trace-formula dispute now has a public, specific form, that 12.5.1.1 sums only interior zeros while the trace it cites runs over the closed strip, with the equivalence above as its consequence, though this is a structural defect and not the numerical counterexample reported on the Zulip (EG4 remains open on that ask); the appendix errata have a second, larger list beside them, 21 of the 44 overlapping earlier reports, still unchecked by a specialist (EG5 unchanged). The report's own list of what is "not yet" proved is the honest part of the page and is the part this record relies on. A rerun of the 531 standalone sources under a pre-registration is feasible and would make the receipts a second-party fact; it has not been done. The note is one of about ten outside reports on the draft indexed at github.com/mccorvie/riemann-masullo/blob/main/OUTSIDE_REPORTS.md (Yonemoto, Nielsen, Golub/Refine, Nayebi, Goyal, Naslund, Baez and others), most of them AI-generated and most dated 20 to 22 November; this one carries the largest Lean component.

cycles.spoken: On 23 November Hassana Labs published a weekend run of its reinforcement-learning review model over the 940-page draft, with a Lean repository behind it. The model lists 44 defects, 23 new, with repairs, and says the sharpest thing anyone has said about the argument so far: corrected, its central step is equivalent to its conclusion. The remainder in the trace formula is the same across strip widths exactly when no zero is off the line, and that is proved in Lean for any entire function with the right zero count. What is checked is the reviewers' statement about the shape of the argument, under hypotheses; the trace formula itself is neither proved nor refuted on the draft's objects, and the report lists plainly what remains unproved, including the functional equation for any field but Q. It is a report by a model under a company's name, so it closes no gap here. It confirms the placeholders in Chapter 13 and gives the trace-formula dispute a precise public form, which is what the record has been asking for.

background.spoken: The Riemann Hypothesis says every zero of the Riemann zeta function with real part strictly between zero and one has real part one half. The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis says the same of every Hecke L-function of every number field, so for every Dirichlet L-function in particular. The draft's stated generality is all number fields and all unitary Hecke characters.

background.term: The claim by Alessandro Maria Masullo
background.spoken: The draft builds a trace formula for Hecke L-functions of a number field from adelic theta functions, idelic zeta functions, Schauder bases on modulated groups and nuclear operators on Hardy-Sobolev spaces, and labels that formula 12.5.1.1, "the Main Theorem of this work". Chapter 13 is to deduce from it that the zeros lie on the half line, with a multiplicity bound; Chapter 14 discusses why the method does not extend to function fields. As released, Chapter 13 contains the headings of three sections, a restatement of the trace formula with a footnote reading "Correct statement", and a result labelled "Divisor of L(s, chi)" whose statement is a footnote reading "Insert statement" followed by "State and prove the Main Theorems". So the draft states no result about the zeros. The preface says the introduction is unfinished and that the author was to spend a year at Stanford polishing the text. A Lean 4 formalization effort by a third party (github.com/mccorvie/riemann-masullo) started the day of release, logs ten appendix statements it reports as false as stated and about thirty imprecisions, none yet reviewed by a specialist, and paused the same day after a report on the Lean Zulip that an AI-assisted reading found a counterexample to the trace formula; that counterexample has not been posted.
